citeinfo.othercit: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission and NCCGIA distributes this dataset.

descript.abstract: Over 2,000,000 acres of public and private lands in North Carolina, designated as "game lands", are managed by the Wildlife Resources Commission for public hunting, trapping and inland fishing. This dataset shows detailed game land information, including individual tracts, game land types and designations. Hunting on the Roanoke River National Wildlife Refuge is managed by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service and the N.C. Wildlife Resources Com­mission through a joint venture. Additional regulations apply to the Roanoke River National Wildlife Refuge. General game land regulations are available at http://www.eregulations.com/northcarolina/hunting-fishing/general-game-lands-regulations/. Individual maps are available at https://www.ncwildlife.org/Hunting/Where-To-Hunt-Shoot/Public-Places.

attracc.attraccr: The NC Wildlife Resources Commission originally delineated the Game Lands onto mylar overlays mapped at 1:100,000 scale. NC CGIA digitized these areas and attributed them with Game Land name, type, owner, and public or private status. Attributes were checked by WRC staff. Subsequent updates and additions were made as previously outlined.

dataqual.logic: Using ESRI's ARC/INFO GIS software, the dataset was built for arc and polygon topology using the "build" command. The data set was then cleaned with a fuzzy tolerance of 1 foot. Topology has not been edited since the last build or clean. Subsequent additions have been acquired from a combination of county parcel data, digitizing from aerial photos, GPS information, and boundary estimation.
dataqual.complete: These data represent all publicly-owned and managed Game Lands, or those managed cooperatively as Game Lands by the NC Wildlife Resources Commission and as outlined in the "Hunting and Fishing Maps for North Carolina Game Lands" publication.

horizpa.horizpar: Game Lands were originally marked on 1:100,000 USGS dlg overlays, which meet National Map Accuracy Standards, using a best estimate with reference to surrounding features. Boundaries drawn were digitized and check plots used to ensure correct boundary location. Subsequent updates have been incorporated using a variety of methods including GPS, digitizing from aerial photography, and cadastral boundary information.

procstep.procdesc: 2002 boundary updates and additions were incorporated into the file by the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission from various sources: digital data files from diskette, paper maps showing general location (boundaries input from coincident road and hydrography features using Arcedit), paper maps showing metes and bounds coordinates

2001 boundary updates and additions were incorporated into the file by the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission from various sources: digital data files from diskette, paper maps showing general location (boundaries input from coincident road and hydrography features using Arcedit), paper maps showing metes and bounds coordinates

2000 boundary updates and additions were incorporated into the file by the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission from various sources: digital data files from diskette, paper maps showing general location (boundaries input from coincident road and hydrography features using Arcedit), paper maps showing metes and bounds coordinates

1999 boundary updates and additions were incorporated into the file from various sources: digital data files from diskette, paper maps showing general location (boundaries input from coincident road and hydrography features using Arcedit), paper maps showing metes and bounds coordinates (boundaries input using a menu-driven program acquired from the State Property office), etc. The diskettes and maps were supplied by the Wildlife Resources Commission. NC Wildlife Resources Commission supplies CGIA with updates yearly.

The original boundaries of the publicly owned Game Lands in North Carolina were recompiled from the "Hunting and Fishing Maps for North Carolina Game Lands, 1989-90" onto USGS 1:100,000-scale topographic maps. The linework was digitized by NCCGIA then it was checked by light table review. Any necessary corrections were made and new check plots were run. Post processing involved edgematching and mapjoining across map borders to create the final statewide data set.

dataIdInfo.idAbs: This dataset shows public and private lands in North Carolina designated as "game lands" and managed by the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC) for public hunting, trapping, inland fishing and other related activities. This dataset consists of game land boundaries with detailed information such as individual tracts, game land types and hunting designations. General game land regulations are available at http://www.eregulations.com/northcarolina/hunting-fishing/general-game-lands-regulations/. Individual maps are available at https://www.ncwildlife.org/Hunting/Where-To-Hunt-Shoot/Public-Places.

Consts.useLimit: While efforts have been made to ensure that the information provided is accurate as possible, the NCWRC gives no warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability, or completeness of this information. Features and boundaries may be approximate and should not be used for regulatory purposes.
